features.name: Rewards System
features.description: Comprehensive reward system including loot boxes, achievements, and various reward types
features.valueProposition: Students receive tangible and intangible rewards for academic progress
features.userBenefit: Increased motivation through immediate gratification and recognition
details: Loot boxes with artwork, gems, and perks
Multiple reward classifications (scholarships, currency, art, equipment, achievements)
Configurable by school, family, and classroom
Rarity system (Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary)

features.name: Progression & Leveling
features.description: Experience-based leveling system with progress bars and checkpoints
features.valueProposition: Visual representation of academic growth over time
features.userBenefit: Students see tangible progress and unlock new content as they level up
details: Progress bars with checkpoints (similar to Starbucks rewards)
Class category levels (Science, Math, English, etc.)
Evolution points that unlock abilities and content

features.name: Achievements System
features.description: Achievement system for celebrating accomplishments and setting goals
features.valueProposition: Recognition and celebration of student accomplishments
features.userBenefit: Sense of accomplishment, goal guidance, and positive reinforcement
examples: Attend class for a month without missing
Earn >90% on 5 assignments in a row

features.name: Battles & Competition
features.description: Healthy competition features including battles, leaderboards, and rankings
features.valueProposition: Motivation through competitive elements and teamwork

features.name: Social Features
features.description: Social recognition, sharing, and community features
features.valueProposition: Build community and strengthen relationships through shared achievements
features.userBenefit: Social recognition boosts self-esteem and motivation

features.name: Personalization & Customization
features.description: Profile customization, avatars, and personal expression
features.userBenefit: Creative outlet and sense of ownership

features.name: Art & NFTs
features.valueProposition: Unique, collectible rewards that students can own
features.userBenefit: Artistic expression and valuable digital collectibles

features.name: Stores & Marketplace
features.description: Multiple store types for redeeming rewards
features.valueProposition: Choice and autonomy in reward selection
features.userBenefit: Students choose rewards that matter to them

features.name: Parent Communication
features.description: Tools for parent involvement and communication
features.userBenefit: Parents stay informed and can support their children

features.name: Scholarships
features.description: Scholarship opportunities and partial scholarship building
features.valueProposition: Real financial impact for academic success
features.userBenefit: Tangible path to higher education funding

features.name: Quests & Goals
features.description: Goal-setting and quest system for structured progress
features.valueProposition: Clear path to success with guided goals
features.userBenefit: Direction and motivation through structured objectives

features.name: Notifications & Inbox
features.userBenefit: Never miss important updates or achievements

features.name: Sponsorships
features.userBenefit: Access to real-world rewards from brands

dataCollection.description: Ideas for data collection and alternative metrics that could provide value to students and schools

concepts.name: GPA Alternative
concepts.description: Build a more comprehensive student profile than GPA alone. Collect data on engagement, growth, soft skills, and other factors that better represent student potential.
benefits: More holistic view of student ability

concepts.name: Engagement Metrics
concepts.description: Track and quantify student engagement levels over time

concepts.name: Behavioral Data
concepts.description: Track positive behavior incidents and recognition patterns

concepts.name: Growth Patterns
concepts.description: Measure improvement and growth over time, not just absolute performance

dataCollection.privacy: All data collection must prioritize student privacy and comply with FERPA, COPPA, and other regulations

coreFlow.title: Core Starter Product Flow
steps: Event activity is identified from monitoring changes in LMS data (submissions, grades)
Rewardable events are noted and tracked by Expanse
Student reviews activity in Expanse EDU
Student redeems rewards for rewardable event activity
Student receives rewards, recognition, and digital currency
Student engages with other features (battles, customization, social)

parentOnboarding.title: Parent Onboarding Flow
steps: Students invite parents to the application
Parents create account and add information
Parents agree to allow data collection for student
Parents add payment information (optional monthly fee)
Payment configured to go to students for homework completion
Parent configures distribution timing and reward amounts
Parents choose which reward types their student can receive

configurationLevels.description: The software will have various configuration settings at multiple levels
exampleConfigurations: Enable scoring features: Grade-based, Tests, Homework
Reward weights by category (Test vs Homework)

negativeReinforcement.description: Optional negative reinforcement/punishment options for schools that want them
options: Limited earning potential or reduced loot box rewards
negativeReinforcement.note: Focus is on positive reinforcement, but some schools may want negative options available

designConsiderations.description: Key design principles and considerations for product development
organicAdoption: Effective app design should empower students, parents, and teachers to promote the app organically
Features like student benefits for teacher participation and requests for teachers to create stores drive adoption
Visibility into class engagement encourages participation
specialEducation: Special education considerations may vary by district
May need to adjust reward settings for special education students
Consider special education status in reward calculations
classVariations: Gym classes may not have assignments but should still grant experience and rewards
Music and other creative classes have different engagement patterns
Some classes allow online attendance or note-reading instead of in-person
timing: Summer vacation, holidays, exam periods, spring break affect engagement
May have weeks with less participation and work
Time off differs between schools and regions
Apps more likely used during bus rides, between classes, at start of classes, during lunch
policies: Different policies at district, school, and teacher levels
Schools may have different policies on food allowance as rewards
Important options can get rulings at district level
security: Children may not be as secure as parents (leaving screens open, forgetting passwords)
Some features need added protection (PIN, confirmation codes)
Payment, trade, and some rewards require higher security
fairness: Product design should improve educational experience for everyone
Financial situations are a key consideration
Avoid pay-to-win mechanics that disadvantage students
feedback: Praising students indiscriminately can lead to false confidence
Higher grades should earn more experience while still rewarding effort
Problem solving and making mistakes helps learning
internationalDifferences: Country differences in processes, procedures, and interests
Examples: Japan publicly posts grades, physical punishment norms, electronic usage, paper vs online

dataCollectionDetails.description: Detailed data types that may be collected for analytics and personalization
coreData: Parent reward options and student selections

gpaAlternative.description: Rather than comparing students solely based on GPA, compare based on performance relative to peers for clearer insight
gpaAlternative.benefit: Enables teachers to aim for 70-90% as target on challenging homework rather than 100%
